findings.claim: The doctor will fail to start instead of skipping when the versions comparison dependency is absent.
findings.evidence: Acceptance criteria: "Runnable before its dependencies land: each dependent check is `skip` with a reason until then"; `lib/doctor/runtime.mjs` statically imports `compareToTree, parseVersionsToml` from `../../rules/lib/versions-toml.mjs`, so if that dependency has not landed, module loading aborts before `mini-versions-toml` can return `skip`.
findings.suggested_fix: Move the `rules/lib/versions-toml.mjs` import inside `mini-versions-toml.run()` using dynamic `import()` and catch module-not-found to return a `skip` outcome with the dependency reason.

findings.claim: `mini-pk` reports an installed-but-broken `pk` as `warn` unless tests inject a resolver.
findings.evidence: Acceptance criteria 2.1 specifies `mini-pk` and optional components "fail only when the component is present and broken (a spawn that exits non-zero)"; `tools.mjs` creates a default resolver, but then uses `const where = ctx.resolve ? resolve('pk') : null`, so the default resolver is never called after `pk --version` exits non-zero.
findings.suggested_fix: Call `const where = resolve('pk')` unconditionally after the version probe fails, and treat a resolved path as `fail`.

findings.claim: `mini-service-liter-llm` treats a non-200 health response as pass despite the spec requiring non-200 health responses to fail.
findings.evidence: Acceptance criteria: `mini-docker`, `mini-service-*`, `mini-pk` and `mini-sycophancy-correction` shall "fail only when the component is present and broken ... a health endpoint answering non-200"; `mini-service-liter-llm` configures `okStatuses: [200, 401]`, so `/health` returning 401 becomes `pass`.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep `/health` success to 200 only; if a separate authenticated endpoint is probed, model that as a separate check or evidence, not as an accepted health status.

findings.claim: Default repository-root resolution is not Windows-safe because it uses `URL.pathname` instead of `fileURLToPath`.
findings.evidence: `const repoRootDefault = () => path.resolve(new URL('../..', import.meta.url).pathname);` appears in `runtime.mjs` and the same pattern is used in other doctor modules; on Windows a file URL pathname is shaped like `/C:/...`, producing invalid or wrong paths, while the proposal says the doctor runs "on any platform".
findings.suggested_fix: Use `fileURLToPath(new URL('../..', import.meta.url))` and `path.resolve` that result; apply the same fix to `lib/doctor/kbd.mjs`, `lib/doctor/skills.mjs`, and `lib/doctor/scope.mjs`.

findings.claim: Runtime outcome conformance does not enforce that emitted fix actions are implemented by the owning check.
findings.evidence: Acceptance/spec requirement: "Every `actions[]` entry of `kind: 'fix'` names a `fixId` that `fixes` implements"; `outcomeConformance()` only checks `{ kind: 'fix', fixId: <non-empty string> }`, while `scripts/doctor.mjs` calls only `outcomeConformance(outcome, check.id)`, so a check can emit an unimplemented fix action and still be printed as valid.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a check-aware outcome validator, e.g. `checkOutcomeConformance(check, outcome)`, that verifies every emitted `fixId` is in `check.offers` and implemented in `check.fixes`, and use it in `scripts/doctor.mjs`.
